extracted.intended_audience: aspiring journalists, journalism students, editors, and media-literacy learners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journalists and editors to decide which events or stories deserve coverage using seven key newsworthiness criteria. Useful for story selection, editorial judgment, and teaching news judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: How recently an event occurred. The more recent a story, the more interesting to readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A traffic accident is newsworthy immediately but becomes outdated within days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Location-based relevance operating on two levels: Geographical (local events directly affecting an audience's daily life) and Psychological (cultural or emotional closeness that transcends geography).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A water main break disrupting traffic in your city vs. the same incident in a distant country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale of effect measured by how many people are affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A pothole affecting dozens vs. a collapsed bridge affecting hundreds of thousands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Status of people or organizations involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Throwing a shoe at a private citizen goes unreported; throwing one at the President becomes international news.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Unusual
rubrics_metrics.description: Events breaking from expected patterns; notable because they deviate from the ordinary (‘If a dog bites a man, that's not news. But if a man bites a dog, that is news.’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Winning the lottery twice; record-defying achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Strife and power struggles creating natural narrative structure with opposing parties and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Wars, elections, legal battles, protests, sports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories connecting through emotion and empathy rather than scale or status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Rags-to-riches stories, overcoming adversity, reunions, acts of generosity. Can succeed despite lacking timeliness or proximity due to emotional resonance.
